It is an ISO 20022 message that a bank sends to answer an investigation about a payment. The most common investigations it answers are cancellation requests, but it is also used to answer other payment investigations, such as a request to confirm whether a payment was received, or a request to correct payment details. The camt.029 is the second half of a conversation. The first half is the investigation request: a camt.056 FI to FI Payment Cancellation Request or a camt.055 Customer Payment Cancellation Request . entries.title: ISO 20022 Interview Questions
entries.text: ISO 20022 Interview Questions ISO 20022 Interview Questions Q1. Explain ISO 20022 to a non-technical stakeholder. Why did the industry move to it? ISO 20022 is a common language for financial messages. Before it, banks used MT messages, which are short text blocks with limited data. A beneficiary address was four lines of free text, and every bank read it differently. ISO 20022 replaces that with structured data: the address is broken into street, town, country and postcode, and the remittance information is structured so the beneficiary can reconcile automatically. The industry moved because regulators want better data for sanctions screening, corporates want automatic reconciliation, and banks want fewer errors. The move is not just a format change. entries.text: MT to MX Field Mapping MT to MX Field Mapping What it is MT to MX field mapping is the translation of each field in a SWIFT MT message into the equivalent element in an ISO 20022 MX message, and back again. MT messages are the older SWIFT format: fixed text blocks with numbered fields, such as field 59 for the beneficiary. MX messages are the newer ISO 20022 format: structured XML with named elements, such as the Cdtr block for the creditor. Mapping is the core work of the migration from MT to MX. A bank cannot send a pacs.008 until it knows how each MT103 field becomes a pacs.008 element. entries.text: MT to MX Migration MT to MX Migration What it is MT to MX migration is the move from SWIFT MT messages to ISO 20022 MX messages for cross-border payments and reporting. entries.text: Correspondent Banking Explained: How Banks Pay Each Other Across Borders Correspondent Banking Explained: How Banks Pay Each Other Across Borders What it is Correspondent banking is the system that lets banks move money across borders when they do not have a direct relationship with each other. A bank in one country holds an account with a bank in another country. That account is called a nostro account . The bank holding the account is the respondent bank. The bank that holds the account for them is the correspondent bank. When a customer of the respondent bank wants to pay someone in the correspondent bank's country, the respondent bank instructs the correspondent bank to make the payment from the nostro account. The correspondent bank debits the nostro account and pays the beneficiary. This is how most cross-border payments work. Correspondent banking is the backbone of international payments. entries.text: MT101 Explained: The Request for Transfer MT101 Explained: The Request for Transfer What it is The MT101 is the SWIFT message a customer or a bank sends to instruct another bank to debit an account and make one or more payments. It is a request for transfer . Unlike the MT103, which is a single payment instruction from one bank to another, the MT101 is an instruction from a customer to their bank, or from one bank to another bank, to execute payments on their behalf. The MT101 is most commonly used for bulk payments . A company that needs to pay hundreds of suppliers, or pay salaries to thousands of employees, sends a single MT101 containing many individual payment instructions. The bank reads the MT101, debits the company account, and executes each payment. The message carries the instruction to pay, the amount, the currency, who is sending, and who should receive the money. The MT103 is the workhorse of cross-border customer payments. entries.text: MT202 COV Explained: The Cover Payment with Full Transparency MT202 COV Explained: The Cover Payment with Full Transparency What it is The MT202 COV is the SWIFT message a bank sends to move funds as cover for a customer payment, with the full customer details included. COV stands for cover. The MT202 COV is a variant of the MT202. The difference is that the MT202 COV carries fields 50a ordering customer and 59a beneficiary customer , so every bank in the chain can see who is sending the money and who is receiving it. The MT202 COV exists because of a transparency problem. entries.title: MT202 Explained: The General Financial Institution Transfer
entries.text: MT202 Explained: The General Financial Institution Transfer MT202 Explained: The General Financial Institution Transfer What it is The MT202 is the SWIFT message a bank sends to move money to another bank for its own account. It is a general financial institution transfer . Unlike the MT103, which carries a customer payment, the MT202 moves funds between banks themselves. It is used for bank-to-bank transfers, funding a nostro account, settling a position, or paying another bank. The MT202 is also used as a cover payment . When a bank sends a customer payment by the cover method, it sends the MT103 directly to the beneficiary bank and sends an MT202 through the correspondent chain to move the funds. entries.title: Nostro vs Vostro: The Same Account, Two Perspectives
entries.text: Nostro vs Vostro: The Same Account, Two Perspectives Nostro vs Vostro: The Same Account, Two Perspectives What it is Nostro and vostro are two names for the same bank account, seen from different sides. The words come from Latin. Nostro means "ours". Vostro means "yours". A nostro account is an account that a bank holds with a correspondent bank in another country. From the perspective of the bank that owns the account, it is "our account with you". A bank in India that holds a US dollar account with a bank in New York calls that account its nostro account. A vostro account is the same account, seen from the perspective of the bank that holds it for the other bank. From the perspective of the New York bank, the Indian bank's account is a vostro account, meaning "your account with us". It is the same account. The name changes depending on who is talking. Why it matters Nostro and vostro accounts are the foundation of correspondent banking and cross-border payments. Every time your bank

entries.title: OUR, SHA and BEN Explained
entries.text: OUR, SHA and BEN Explained OUR, SHA and BEN Explained What it is OUR, SHA, and BEN are the three charge options for a cross-border payment. They decide who pays the charges that the banks in the payment chain apply. The option is agreed between the sender and their bank before the payment is sent, and it is carried in the payment message so that every bank in the chain knows who should pay it. The three options work like this: - OUR means the sender pays all the charges. Every bank in the chain charges the sender, and the beneficiary receives the full amount. In the MT103, this is field 71A with the code OUR. In the pacs.008, it is the charge bearer code DEBT , which means the charges are borne by the debtor. - SHA means the charges are shared. Each bank charges its own customer: the ordering bank charges the sender, and the beneficiary bank charges the beneficiary. No bank deducts its charge from the payment amount. In the MT103, this is field 71A with the code SHA. In the pacs.008,

entries.title: Serial vs Cover Payments: Two Ways to Move Money Across Borders
entries.text: Serial vs Cover Payments: Two Ways to Move Money Across Borders Serial vs Cover Payments: Two Ways to Move Money Across Borders What it is When a bank sends a cross-border payment, the funds have to travel from the sender bank to the beneficiary bank. There are two ways to do this: the serial method and the cover method . The choice affects speed, cost, transparency, and risk. In the serial method , a single message travels from bank to bank along the chain. Each bank receives the payment instruction, deducts its charges if any, and forwards the remaining amount to the next bank. The instruction and the funds travel together, hop by hop, until they reach the beneficiary bank. In the cover method , two messages travel separately. The payment instruction the MT103 or pacs.008 goes directly from the sender bank to the beneficiary bank. The funds travel separately through the correspondent banking chain, carried by a cover message the MT202 COV or pacs.009 . The beneficiary bank receives

entries.title: SWIFT gpi Explained
entries.text: SWIFT gpi Explained SWIFT gpi Explained What it is SWIFT gpi Global Payments Innovation is a service that runs on top of the SWIFT network and gives banks and their customers end-to-end visibility of a cross-border payment. Before gpi, a cross-border payment disappeared into a chain of correspondent banks. The ordering bank could not see where the payment was, how long it would take, or what charges had been deducted. The customer asking "where is my payment" got no useful answer. gpi changed that by adding tracking, speed commitments, and fee transparency to the same SWIFT messages banks already used. gpi is not a new payment system and it is not a new message type. It is a set of rules and services that gpi member banks agree to follow. The core of it is the UETR , the Unique End-to-end Transaction Reference, a 36-character identifier that stays with a payment for its whole journey. Every bank in the chain includes the UETR in its status reports, so the payment can be followed from

entries.title: SWIFT Payments Explained
entries.text: SWIFT Payments Explained SWIFT Payments Explained What it is A SWIFT payment is a cross-border payment that travels over the SWIFT network. SWIFT is a member-owned cooperative that runs a secure messaging network for financial institutions. More than 11,000 institutions in over 200 countries use it. When a bank sends a payment to a bank in another country, it usually sends the instruction over SWIFT. Three facts about SWIFT surprise most newcomers. First, SWIFT is a messaging network, not a bank . It does not hold money, it does not settle payments, and it does not move funds. It carries instructions between banks. Second, SWIFT does not move the money behind the instruction. The funds move separately, through nostro accounts that banks hold with each other, or through local clearing systems. Third, a SWIFT payment is a chain, not a single hop. The instruction usually passes through two, three or four banks before it reaches the beneficiary. The messages that carry SWIFT payments have

entries.title: UETR Explained
entries.text: UETR Explained UETR Explained What it is The UETR Unique End-to-end Transaction Reference is a 36-character identifier that stays with a cross-border payment for its whole journey, from the ordering bank to the beneficiary bank. It is assigned once, by the bank that first instructs the payment, and it never changes. Every bank in the chain carries the same UETR in its messages about that payment, so the whole journey can be stitched together from the separate messages each bank sends. The UETR is a UUID version 4 . It has five groups of hexadecimal characters separated by hyphens, in the pattern 8-4-4-4-12. An example looks like this: 6f8e2b1a-3c4d-4e5f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b . The first group has 8 characters, then three groups of 4, then a final group of 12. The 13th character is always 4 , which marks it as a version 4 UUID, and the first character of the fourth group is 8 , 9 , a , or b , which marks the UUID variant. These fixed positions are how a system can tell a well-formed UETR

entries.title: ACH vs RTGS
entries.text: ACH vs RTGS ACH vs RTGS What it is ACH Automated Clearing House and RTGS Real Time Gross Settlement are two different ways of moving money between banks. They solve the same problem, getting funds from one bank account to another, but they do it in opposite ways. An ACH system collects payment instructions over a period, batches them together, nets the amounts off against each other, and settles the net result later. An RTGS system settles each payment individually, in real time, as soon as it is received. In the US, the main ACH operator is Nacha , and the main RTGS system is Fedwire , run by the Federal Reserve. In the UK, Bacs is the ACH equivalent and CHAPS is the RTGS system. In India, NEFT is a deferred net settlement system similar in spirit to ACH and RTGS is the real time gross settlement system, both run by the Reserve Bank of India. Why it matters Choosing between ACH and RTGS is one of the first decisions in any payment design. The choice decides when the beneficiary gets

entries.title: CHAPS Explained
entries.text: CHAPS Explained CHAPS Explained What it is CHAPS Clearing House Automated Payment System is the UK's high value, same day payment system. It is a real time gross settlement system operated by the Bank of England . It is used for large payments where same day finality matters: house purchases, business to business payments, tax payments, and financial market settlements. There is no upper limit on a CHAPS payment. There is no lower limit set by the scheme, although banks typically use CHAPS for payments above 10,000 pounds because of the cost. CHAPS is operated by the Bank of England and is one of the largest high value payment systems in the world by value. Why it matters CHAPS is where the money is. Although it processes far fewer payments than Faster Payments or Bacs, the total value settled through CHAPS each day is enormous, running into hundreds of billions of pounds. A single CHAPS payment can be worth more than a whole day of Faster Payments volume. For a business analyst,

entries.title: Clearing vs Settlement
entries.text: Clearing vs Settlement Clearing vs Settlement What it is Clearing and settlement are two different stages in a payment. They are often mentioned together, but they are not the same thing, and confusing them is one of the most common mistakes in payments. Clearing is the exchange, validation, and sorting of payment instructions between banks. It is the process of agreeing what is owed, to whom, and by whom. Settlement is the actual movement of funds between banks to discharge those obligations. Clearing answers the question "what do we owe each other?" Settlement answers the question "how do we pay it?" In some systems, clearing and settlement happen almost together. In others, they happen hours or days apart. Understanding the gap between them is essential for understanding payment risk, liquidity, and reconciliation. Why it matters The gap between clearing and settlement is where payment risk lives. If a bank credits a beneficiary during clearing, before settlement has happened, it

entries.title: Duplicate Payments Explained
entries.text: Duplicate Payments Explained Duplicate Payments Explained What it is A duplicate payment is a payment that is sent twice when it should have been sent once. The customer intended one payment, but the bank sent two, and the beneficiary received the money twice. The second payment is the duplicate. It is a real payment, made from the customer's account, and getting the money back requires a return or a recall. Duplicates are one of the most common payment errors, and one of the most costly. The customer loses money temporarily, the beneficiary has funds that are not theirs, and the bank has to recover the duplicate through a process that can take days. A duplicate also creates a reconciliation problem, because the customer's records show one payment and the bank's records show two. Duplicates happen in different ways, but they share a cause: the same logical payment is submitted to the payment system more than once, and the system does not recognise the second submission as a copy of

entries.title: Faster Payments Explained
entries.text: Faster Payments Explained Faster Payments Explained What it is Faster Payments is the UK's near real time payment system. It lets people and businesses send money between UK bank accounts in seconds, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. It is operated by Pay.UK and is used for personal transfers, bill payments, salary payments, and business payments. The maximum value for a single Faster Payments transaction is 1 million pounds. In practice, most banks set their own lower limits for individual customers, often between 10,000 and 100,000 pounds per payment, depending on the channel and the customer. Faster Payments is not the same as CHAPS . CHAPS is the UK's high value real time gross settlement system, used for large payments such as house purchases. Faster Payments is for the high volume, lower value, near real time payments that people make every day. Why it matters Faster Payments changed what UK customers expect from a bank. Before it launched in 2008, a bank transfer took up to three

entries.title: Idempotency in Payment APIs Explained
entries.text: Idempotency in Payment APIs Explained Idempotency in Payment APIs Explained What it is Idempotency means that sending the same request more than once has the same effect as sending it once. In a payment API, an idempotent request can be retried safely: if the first attempt is lost, the client can send the request again, and the payment will be made once, not twice. Without idempotency, a retry is a gamble. The client does not know whether the first request was processed, and sending it again risks paying twice. Idempotency is delivered through an idempotency key . The key is a unique value that the client generates for each logical payment, usually a UUID version 4, and sends with the payment request in a header, commonly called Idempotency-Key . The key identifies the payment request, not the payment itself. One key means one payment. If the server sees the same key again, it knows the request has already been processed and returns the original response instead of making a second

entries.title: Payment APIs Explained
entries.text: Payment APIs Explained Payment APIs Explained What it is A payment API Application Programming Interface lets one system ask another system to do something with a payment, using a defined set of requests and responses over the internet. Instead of uploading a file or typing into a screen, a customer, a partner, or an internal system sends a structured request to the bank's API, and the bank responds with a structured result. Payment APIs are used for payment initiation starting a payment , status enquiry asking where a payment is , account information checking a balance or a statement , and webhooks receiving a notification when something changes . They are the foundation of open banking, of embedded finance, and of most modern fintech products. A payment API is not a single thing. It is a set of endpoints, each of which does one job, with defined request and response formats, authentication rules, and error handling. Why it matters APIs are how modern payments work. A marketplace

entries.title: Payment Exception Handling
entries.text: Payment Exception Handling Payment Exception Handling What it is Payment exception handling is the process of dealing with payments that do not complete normally. An exception is any payment that fails validation, is rejected by a clearing system, is returned, is recalled, is delayed, is duplicated, or is stuck in an unknown state. Exceptions are a normal part of payment operations. A bank that processes millions of payments a day will have thousands of exceptions. The quality of a bank's exception handling determines how quickly customers get their money back, how much manual work operations teams do, and how much the bank loses to errors. The exception lifecycle has five stages: detection finding the exception , classification understanding what type it is , investigation finding the root cause , resolution fixing it: repair, return, recall, or reverse , and prevention changing something so it does not happen again . Why it matters Exceptions are where customers form their opinion

entries.title: Payment Gateway vs Payment Hub
entries.text: Payment Gateway vs Payment Hub Payment Gateway vs Payment Hub What it is A payment gateway and a payment hub sound similar, but they solve different problems for different customers. Confusing them is one of the most common errors in payments conversations, and it leads to requirements that ask the wrong system to do the wrong job. A payment gateway is the merchant-facing front door for accepting payments. When a customer pays on a website or in an app, the gateway takes the card details, checks them, and routes the payment to the merchant's acquirer. It is built for merchants: online shops, subscription businesses, marketplaces, and apps. Examples are the checkout services offered by Stripe, Adyen, and Checkout.com. A payment hub is the bank-side central system that processes payments for the bank itself. It receives payment instructions from all the bank's channels, validates them, enriches them, routes them to the right clearing system, and tracks them through to settlement. It is

entries.title: Payment Hub Architecture
entries.text: Payment Hub Architecture Payment Hub Architecture What it is A payment hub is the central system in a bank that receives payment instructions from all channels, validates them, enriches them, routes them to the right clearing system, and tracks them through to settlement and reconciliation. It is the single place where every payment in the bank passes through, regardless of whether it started in a mobile app, a branch, a corporate file, or an API. The hub sits between the channels where customers instruct payments and the clearing systems where payments are settled . Below the hub are the core banking system which holds the accounts , the nostro accounts which fund cross border payments , and the ledger which records everything . Around the hub are the supporting services: sanctions screening, fraud detection, liquidity management, and the exceptions function. A bank without a hub has separate payment systems for each channel and each rail. A payment from a mobile app goes through one

entries.title: Payment Lifecycle Explained
entries.text: Payment Lifecycle Explained Payment Lifecycle Explained What it is The payment lifecycle is the complete journey of a payment from the moment it is instructed to the moment it is fully reconciled. It has seven distinct stages, and each stage is a separate event with its own timing, its own system, and its own risks. The stages are: 1. Initiation. The customer instructs the payment. 2. Processing. The bank validates, enriches, and routes the payment. 3. Clearing. The payment instruction is exchanged and validated between banks. 4. Settlement. Funds move between banks to discharge the obligation. 5. Beneficiary credit. The beneficiary's bank credits the beneficiary's account. 6. Ledger posting. The bank records the payment in its ledger. 7. Reconciliation. The bank matches the payment against clearing confirmations, settlement entries, and ledger postings to confirm everything agrees. These stages are not interchangeable. A payment can be initiated but not processed. It can be processed

entries.title: Payment Orchestration
entries.text: Payment Orchestration Payment Orchestration What it is Payment orchestration is the intelligent management of how a payment moves from instruction to settlement. It decides which route a payment takes, which provider or clearing system to use, what happens if the first choice fails, and how to optimise for cost, speed, and success rate. Orchestration sits above the payment hub. The hub processes the payment. The orchestrator decides the best path for it. In a simple bank, the hub has a static routing table and the payment always takes the same route. In an orchestrated setup, the route is chosen dynamically based on real time data: the cost of each route, the speed, the current success rate, the time of day, and the payment's own characteristics. Orchestration is most common in payment service providers and fintechs that route payments across multiple providers. It is increasingly used by banks that operate in many countries and need to choose between several correspondent banks and

entries.title: Payment Processing Engine Explained
entries.text: Payment Processing Engine Explained Payment Processing Engine Explained What it is A payment processing engine is the component that executes a payment: it takes an instruction, runs it through the lifecycle, and produces the result. It is the part of a payment system that actually does the work, step by step, and it is distinct from the payment hub , which is the whole system around it. Think of the hub as the building and the engine as the machinery inside it. The hub provides the channels, the connections to clearing systems, the supporting services, and the monitoring. The engine provides the state machine that moves a payment from received to settled, the validation that checks it, the ledger posting that records it, and the retry and recovery logic that handles failures. An engine can sit inside a hub, or it can stand alone. A small fintech may run a single engine that processes all its payments. A large bank runs several engines, one per product or per rail, inside a hub that

entries.title: Payment Repair Explained
entries.text: Payment Repair Explained Payment Repair Explained What it is Payment repair is the manual work of fixing a payment that failed automated processing and putting it back on its journey. When a payment cannot be processed straight through, the payment hub moves it into a repair queue , where an operations analyst reviews the problem, corrects the payment, and releases it. The payment is repaired, not rejected, because the underlying instruction is usually valid. Something about the data is wrong, and a person needs to fix it. A repair queue is not a single queue. A bank typically runs several, each for a different type of problem. A data repair queue holds payments with missing or invalid fields. A compliance queue holds payments stopped by a sanctions or fraud screening hit. An account repair queue holds payments where the beneficiary account cannot be found. Each queue has its own team, its own service level, and its own rules about what an analyst is allowed to change. Repair is the

entries.title: Payment Routing
entries.text: Payment Routing Payment Routing What it is Payment routing is the process of deciding which path a payment takes from the sending bank to the receiving bank. The route determines which clearing system, which correspondent bank, and which settlement account are used. Routing is driven by routing tables and static data maintained by the bank's payments team. Every payment has a route. A domestic payment in the UK might route through Faster Payments or CHAPS. A euro payment might route through SEPA or SWIFT. A cross border payment might route through one correspondent bank or a chain of three. The routing decision is made by the payment hub, based on the payment's characteristics and the bank's routing rules. Why it matters Routing decides the cost, the speed, and the reliability of a payment. A payment routed through the wrong correspondent costs more and takes longer. A payment routed to a clearing system that is closed for the day will wait until the next business day. A payment

entries.title: Payment Status State Machine Explained
entries.text: Payment Status State Machine Explained Payment Status State Machine Explained What it is A payment status state machine is the formal model of the lifecycle of a payment. It defines the states a payment can be in, the transitions that move it from one state to another, and who is allowed to make each move. Every payment in a bank follows the same state machine, from the moment it is received to the moment it reaches a final state. A typical payment state machine has these states: - Received. The payment instruction has arrived at the bank and been recorded, but no checks have run yet. - Validated. The payment has passed the bank's validation checks: the account and beneficiary details, the amount, the currency, the value date, and the sanctions and fraud screening. - Queued. The payment has passed validation and is waiting to be sent, usually because it is held for a cut-off time, a value date, or a batch. - Sent. The payment instruction has left the bank and is travelling to the next

entries.title: RTP Explained
entries.text: RTP Explained RTP Explained What it is RTP Real Time Payments is the real time payment system for the United States, operated by The Clearing House TCH . It lets banks send and receive payments in real time, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, with immediate confirmation and final settlement. The transaction limit for RTP is 10 million dollars. This was raised from 1 million dollars on 9 February 2025, reflecting the growing use of RTP for larger business payments. RTP is separate from FedNow , which is the Federal Reserve's real time payment system. Both are real time payment systems in the US, but they are operated by different organisations and banks may connect to one or both. Why it matters The US was late to real time payments compared to the UK, Europe, and India. RTP, launched in 2017, and FedNow, launched in 2023, changed that. Businesses can now pay suppliers instantly, workers can receive wages in real time, and consumers can send money to each other immediately, at any time.

entries.title: SEPA Explained
entries.text: SEPA Explained SEPA Explained What it is SEPA Single Euro Payments Area is the system that lets euro payments move between bank accounts across Europe as easily as domestic payments move inside one country. It covers 36 countries: the 27 EU member states plus the UK, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, Monaco, San Marino, Andorra, and Vatican City. SEPA has two main instruments. SCT SEPA Credit Transfer moves money from a payer to a payee. SDD SEPA Direct Debit lets a payee pull money from a payer's account with a mandate. Both are governed by rulebooks published by the European Payments Council EPC . SEPA is not a single system run by one operator. It is a set of rules, standards, and schemes. Banks and payment service providers implement the schemes, and clearing and settlement mechanisms CSMs such as EBA Clearing STEP2 and the Eurosystem's TARGET Services move the funds. Why it matters Before SEPA, a euro payment from Germany to France was a cross border payment: slow,

entries.title: SEPA Instant Explained
entries.text: SEPA Instant Explained SEPA Instant Explained What it is SEPA Instant Credit Transfer SCT Inst is the instant payment scheme for euro payments. A payment instructed under SCT Inst must reach the payee's bank within 10 seconds, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year. There is no cut-off, no business day, and no waiting until morning. SCT Inst is governed by a rulebook from the European Payments Council EPC . The settlement happens through TIPS TARGET Instant Payment Settlement , the Eurosystem's instant settlement service, or through other clearing and settlement mechanisms that support instant payments. The Instant Payments Regulation, Regulation EU 2024/886 , makes instant payments mandatory for banks in the euro area. It also makes Verification of Payee VoP mandatory, so the payer is shown the name matching the account before the payment is sent. The SCT Inst amount cap was removed by the 2025 rulebook. Previously, SCT Inst payments were capped at 100,000 euros. From 5

entries.title: Straight-Through Processing (STP) Explained
entries.text: Straight-Through Processing (STP) Explained Straight-Through Processing STP Explained What it is Straight-through processing , or STP , means a payment is processed from instruction to settlement without any manual intervention. The payment is received, validated, screened, routed, and sent by systems, with no person touching it at any point. A payment that goes straight through is faster, cheaper, and less likely to go wrong than a payment that stops for manual work. The STP rate is the share of payments that go straight through. It is calculated as the number of payments processed with no manual intervention, divided by the total number of payments, expressed as a percentage. A bank that processes 10,000 payments in a day and repairs 800 of them has an STP rate of 92 percent. The other 8 percent went to a repair queue, a compliance review, or an exception. STP is not a single number for a whole bank. It is measured by channel, by currency, by corridor, and by payment type. A

entries.title: TARGET Services Explained
entries.text: TARGET Services Explained TARGET Services Explained What it is TARGET Services are the Eurosystem's market infrastructure services: the systems that settle payments, securities, and collateral in central bank money in the euro area. The Eurosystem is the European Central Bank plus the national central banks of the countries that use the euro. TARGET Services are operated by the Eurosystem, and they are the backbone of the euro payment system. There are four TARGET Services. T2 is the real-time gross settlement system for large-value euro payments. TIPS is the instant payment settlement service. T2S is the securities settlement platform. ECMS is the collateral management system. Together they cover the full lifecycle: a payment settles in T2 or TIPS, a securities trade settles in T2S, and the collateral that supports all of it is managed in ECMS. The name TARGET has been used since 1999, when the first TARGET system went live with the euro. The services have been rebuilt and

entries.title: UPI Explained
entries.text: UPI Explained UPI Explained What it is UPI Unified Payments Interface is India's real time payment system for person to person and person to merchant payments. It is operated by the National Payments Corporation of India NPCI . It lets anyone with a bank account and a mobile phone send and receive money instantly, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, using a mobile app. UPI works through a Virtual Payment Address VPA , such as name@bankname, so people do not need to share their account number and IFSC code. It also works with QR codes, phone numbers, and account numbers. The standard transaction limit is 1 lakh rupees per transaction, although higher limits apply for certain categories such as capital markets, insurance, and tax payments. UPI is the largest real time payment system in the world by volume, processing billions of transactions every month. It runs on top of the IMPS Immediate Payment Service rails for settlement between banks. Why it matters UPI changed how India pays. Before

entries.title: Six PACS messages that run every flow
entries.text: Six PACS messages that run every flow Foundations The PACS family is the working vocabulary of ISO 20022 payments: pacs.008 carries the customer credit transfer, pacs.009 moves funds between financial institutions, pacs.002 reports status, pacs.004 returns a settled payment, pacs.028 requests status, and pacs.029 resolves an investigation. Master these six first, because every flow in this product is described in their terms. Master these six first, because every flow in this product is described in their terms.

entries.title: ISO 20022: data, automation and control
entries.text: ISO 20022: data, automation and control Foundations ISO 20022 is a data standard before it is a format change: structured data travels with the payment, so validation, screening and reconciliation can run straight through without manual rework. Richer data also gives every party visibility across the full lifecycle, from initiation to final status. Treat the message as the control point, not the envelope, and the automation follows. Treat the message as the control point, not the envelope, and the automation follows.

entries.title: SEPA reject vs return: the stage decides
entries.text: SEPA reject vs return: the stage decides Foundations In SEPA, timing is the whole distinction: a reject happens before settlement and is reported with pacs.002, while a return happens after settlement and uses pacs.004. The first diagnostic question on any failed SEPA payment is therefore the stage at which it failed. Pin the stage first, and the handling path follows. Pin the stage first, and the handling path follows.

entries.title: Card payment: authorize, clear, settle
entries.text: Card payment: authorize, clear, settle Foundations A card payment runs in three distinct stages. At authorization the issuer verifies the card, the balance, fraud signals, and the PIN, CVV, or 3DS check; clearing is the network exchanging records between banks; and settlement is the point funds actually move to the merchant. Authorization is permission, clearing is the record, and settlement is the money, and only the last closes the payment. Authorization is permission, clearing is the record, and settlement is the money, and only the last closes the payment.

entries.title: The payment map only works connected
entries.text: The payment map only works connected Foundations ISO 20022 and SWIFT knowledge alone does not make a payments expert. Real expertise connects the payment lifecycle, cards, rails, clearing and settlement, fraud and AML, APIs and the end-to-end journey, because each piece only makes sense through its joins to the others. Learn the connections, not the components in isolation, and the domain starts to behave as one system. Learn the connections, not the components in isolation, and the domain starts to behave as one system.

entries.title: Payments is one system, not silos
entries.text: Payments is one system, not silos Foundations Payments is one connected system, not a set of separate topics. Rails, cards, ISO 8583 and ISO 20022, APIs, PCI and tokenization, the lifecycle, compliance and emerging payments each touch the rest, so study every piece by asking how it connects. A professional who maps the joins will always outperform one who memorises the parts. A professional who maps the joins will always outperform one who memorises the parts.

entries.title: Cross-border: speed, cost, control, clarity
entries.text: Cross-border: speed, cost, control, clarity Foundations Cross-border payments join different countries and different systems into a single flow, and the test is the same everywhere: speed, cost, compliance and transparency. A payment that is fast but opaque, or cheap but non-compliant, fails that test whatever the corridor. Judge every cross-border design on all four together, never on one alone. Judge every cross-border design on all four together, never on one alone.

entries.title: Can a Letter of Credit go fully digital?
entries.text: Can a Letter of Credit go fully digital? Foundations A Letter of Credit is a trade finance instrument that has traditionally run on paper, yet a fully digital LC shows even the most document-heavy payment product can run end to end without it. For a BA, the real work is tracing what changes in process, data and controls when the paper goes away. Digitisation is a redesign of the control model, not a scan of the documents. Digitisation is a redesign of the control model, not a scan of the documents.

entries.title: Asia banking: real-time, API-first, cloud
entries.text: Asia banking: real-time, API-first, cloud Foundations Banking in Asia is moving to real-time payments, API-first design, cloud and ISO 20022, and that shift opens a new engineering opportunity for people who understand both technology and the banking transaction lifecycle. The winners are the ones who can bridge the two. The winners are the ones who can bridge the two.

entries.title: Direct debit: the creditor pulls on the due date
entries.text: Direct debit: the creditor pulls on the due date Foundations Direct debit is the collection method European businesses rely on for recurring payments such as subscriptions and utility bills, because the creditor initiates the pull on the due date instead of waiting for the debtor to pay. That creditor-driven timing is the whole point: it puts the collection schedule under the creditor's control and cuts late payment. It only works when the mandate, the Creditor Identifier and the scheme rules are all set up correctly, so a collection flow has to be designed around those three prerequisites from the start. It only works when the mandate, the Creditor Identifier and the scheme rules are all set up correctly, so a collection flow has to be designed around those three prerequisites from the start.

entries.title: Creditor and Creditor Identifier in SDD
entries.text: Creditor and Creditor Identifier in SDD Foundations In SEPA Direct Debit the creditor is the business collecting the money, and the Creditor Identifier is the unique code that identifies that creditor across the scheme. The identifier travels with every collection, so the debtor bank and the debtor can both recognise who is pulling the funds. No correct identifier means no collection can be initiated or matched to the right creditor, so the identifier is a gating data item, not a label. No correct identifier means no collection can be initiated or matched to the right creditor, so the identifier is a gating data item, not a label.

entries.title: The four-corner model of a direct debit
entries.text: The four-corner model of a direct debit Foundations A SEPA Direct Debit moves through four corners: the creditor, the creditor PSP, the clearing and settlement mechanism, and the debtor PSP with the debtor. The creditor sends the collection file to its PSP, the PSP passes it to the clearing system, and the debtor PSP debits the debtor account on the due date. Each corner owns a distinct responsibility, so when a collection fails the model pinpoints exactly which party owns the failure. Each corner owns a distinct responsibility, so when a collection fails the model pinpoints exactly which party owns the failure.

entries.title: Due date, debit date and settlement date
entries.text: Due date, debit date and settlement date Foundations The due date is the date the creditor wants the money, the debit date is the date the debtor account is actually debited, and the settlement date is the date the funds move between the banks. The three dates often fall on the same day, but they can split apart when a PSP is closed or the clearing system is unavailable. Confusing them produces wrong value dating and reconciliation breaks, so each date must be tracked as a separate fact. Confusing them produces wrong value dating and reconciliation breaks, so each date must be tracked as a separate fact.

entries.title: Pre-notification is not collection submission
entries.text: Pre-notification is not collection submission Foundations Pre-notification is the notice the creditor sends the debtor before the collection, stating the amount and the date, while collection submission is the creditor PSP sending the collection file into the scheme for processing. The two steps run on different timelines, and generating the file is not the same as notifying the customer. If the amount changes and the pre-notification is not updated, the debtor can dispute the collection, so the notice and the file must stay in step. If the amount changes and the pre-notification is not updated, the debtor can dispute the collection, so the notice and the file must stay in step.

entries.title: Pre-notification: 14 days unless agreed otherwise
entries.text: Pre-notification: 14 days unless agreed otherwise Foundations The scheme expects the creditor to notify the debtor before each collection, usually 14 calendar days in advance, unless creditor and debtor have agreed a different timeline. Any agreed alternative must be evidenced, so the creditor can prove the debtor accepted a shorter notice period. A shorter notice with no agreement behind it leaves the collection open to dispute, so the evidence is as much part of the collection as the notice itself. A shorter notice with no agreement behind it leaves the collection open to dispute, so the evidence is as much part of the collection as the notice itself.

entries.title: Calendar days are not banking business days
entries.text: Calendar days are not banking business days Foundations Some scheme timelines run in calendar days and others in banking business days, and applying the wrong calendar produces the wrong date. Pre-notification, refund windows and scheme timelines each specify which calendar applies, so no two timelines can be assumed to work the same way. The discipline is simple: check the calendar for each timeline before computing any date. The discipline is simple: check the calendar for each timeline before computing any date.

entries.title: Three calendars govern one collection
entries.text: Three calendars govern one collection Foundations A direct debit collection depends on three calendars at once: the creditor PSP, the debtor PSP, and the clearing and settlement mechanism. If any one of them is closed on the due date, the collection cannot complete that day, even when the other two are open. Planning on a single calendar, such as only the creditor's own business calendar, is what produces late debits. Planning on a single calendar, such as only the creditor's own business calendar, is what produces late debits.

entries.title: Why cross-border still lags domestic instant
entries.text: Why cross-border still lags domestic instant Foundations A domestic instant payment moves inside one system under one set of rules, while a cross-border payment passes through several payment service providers, currency conversions, compliance checks and settlement systems. Each hop adds time, and the hops depend on each other's operating hours. The chain of dependencies is the reason cross-border payments stay slower even when every individual leg is fast. The chain of dependencies is the reason cross-border payments stay slower even when every individual leg is fast.

entries.title: UETR: one reference across every hop
entries.text: UETR: one reference across every hop Foundations The UETR is a unique end-to-end transaction reference that stays with a payment across every bank and system it passes through. It lets any party trace the payment and ask each hop for its status using the same reference. A UETR proves the payment exists and can be tracked, but it does not by itself prove where the money is or that it settled, so tracking and settlement evidence must never be confused. A UETR proves the payment exists and can be tracked, but it does not by itself prove where the money is or that it settled, so tracking and settlement evidence must never be confused.

entries.title: Instant credit is not instant settlement
entries.text: Instant credit is not instant settlement Foundations When a customer sends an instant payment, the beneficiary may see the credit within seconds, but the banks behind the payment may still settle between themselves later. The customer experience, the scheme processing and the settlement finality are three different things that do not always happen at the same moment. A payment can look instant to the customer while the interbank settlement is still pending, so the screen is never proof of finality. A payment can look instant to the customer while the interbank settlement is still pending, so the screen is never proof of finality.

entries.title: G20 targets for cross-border payments
entries.text: G20 targets for cross-border payments Foundations The G20 set targets for cross-border payments covering speed, cost, transparency and access, so that sending money across borders becomes cheaper, faster and easier to track. These are goals for the industry, not guarantees for a single payment, and each target needs concrete product and operational measures to be met. A business analyst uses the objectives to judge whether a corridor design is actually improving the customer outcome, which is the only test that matters. A business analyst uses the objectives to judge whether a corridor design is actually improving the customer outcome, which is the only test that matters.

entries.title: Turn scheme rules into buildable requirements
entries.text: Turn scheme rules into buildable requirements Foundations Payment scheme rules are written in technical language, but developers and business users need them as a clear trigger, decision, rule, timeline and system behaviour. Translating a rule into what happens, when, and what the system must do is what makes it buildable. Jargon left in a requirement produces a system that does the wrong thing confidently, so plain, precise wording is a quality control, not a courtesy. Jargon left in a requirement produces a system that does the wrong thing confidently, so plain, precise wording is a quality control, not a courtesy.

entries.title: camt.052, camt.053, camt.054: three views, one account
entries.text: camt.052, camt.053, camt.054: three views, one account Foundations Liquidity management turns on when funds are available, not only how much, and camt.052, camt.053 and camt.054 each give a different view of the same account. The camt.052 account report shows the position accumulated so far today, the camt.053 statement shows the end-of-day position, and the camt.054 notification reports individual debits and credits as they occur. With a EUR 9 million opening balance, EUR 4 million coming in and a EUR 6 million payment to make, the intraday view shows EUR 7 million only if the incoming payment arrives in time, so relying on camt.053 alone misses the intraday picture entirely. With a EUR 9 million opening balance, EUR 4 million coming in and a EUR 6 million payment to make, the intraday view shows EUR 7 million only if the incoming payment arrives in time, so relying on camt.053 alone misses the intraday picture entirely.

entries.title: pain.001 for ten: three on-us payments need no pacs.008
entries.text: pain.001 for ten: three on-us payments need no pacs.008 Foundations A pain.001 file promises a batch of payments, yet not every payment in the file becomes a pacs.008: when a corporate submits 10 payments and only 7 pacs.008 messages reach the next bank, the other 3 are on-us payments, where sender and beneficiary hold accounts with the same bank and the payment is handled internally. Counting only pacs.008 messages shows 7 payments and suggests 3 are missing, while comparing the file total with the message count reveals the 3 on-us payments and explains the gap. A pain.001 is therefore a promise that payments will be made, not a guarantee of a pacs.008 for each one. A pain.001 is therefore a promise that payments will be made, not a guarantee of a pacs.008 for each one.

entries.title: Payment confirmation: trust the reply, not the debit
entries.text: Payment confirmation: trust the reply, not the debit Foundations Confirmation in payments comes from the receiving side, not from the debit: on PhonePe, Payment Successful appears only after the beneficiary bank confirms the credit and UPI passes that reply back. In UPI the reply is RespPay, carrying credited or failed, and ISO 20022 schemes carry the same step under a different name, pacs.002, the Payment Status Report. A payment therefore stands confirmed only when the receiving side returns a status, so trust the confirmation, not the debit. A payment therefore stands confirmed only when the receiving side returns a status, so trust the confirmation, not the debit.

entries.title: Open Finance consent: know what you are agreeing to
entries.text: Open Finance consent: know what you are agreeing to Foundations Consent to access financial information is not simply a yes to everything: when applying for a loan and seeing that request, check who is asking for the data, what data they want, why they need it, how often they will access it, and how long the consent is valid, because two services can need very different data for different purposes. Under India Account Aggregator ecosystem, consent can be revoked, and revoking it can stop further access to the data. Good consent states its purpose and duration plainly, with a clear way to withdraw, in plain language anyone can follow. Good consent states its purpose and duration plainly, with a clear way to withdraw, in plain language anyone can follow.

entries.title: Open Finance: the information moves, the account stays
entries.text: Open Finance: the information moves, the account stays Foundations A salary account with one bank does not stop another bank from offering a competitive loan, because the financial relationship no longer has to sit with a single institution. One customer can hold an account with ICICI, a loan with SBI, insights with CRED and payments with Google Pay, while the salary account stays where it is. What moves between providers is the financial information, and it moves only with the customer consent. That reframes the competitive question: not how to become your bank, but how to become the provider chosen for the next financial need. That reframes the competitive question: not how to become your bank, but how to become the provider chosen for the next financial need.

entries.title: VoP No Match: the payment does not always stop
entries.text: VoP No Match: the payment does not always stop Foundations Verification of Payee tests whether the name the payer gave matches the name the payee bank holds for the account, cutting authorised push payment fraud and misdirected payments. A No Match result does not stop the payment automatically: depending on the bank process, the payer can review and correct the details, or continue knowing the payment may reach the wrong payee. A No Match says only that the name does not match, not whether it is fraud or a simple error, so it needs attention but not automatic rejection, and a BA documenting VoP requirements must capture these rules rather than assume No Match means stop. A No Match says only that the name does not match, not whether it is fraud or a simple error, so it needs attention but not automatic rejection, and a BA documenting VoP requirements must capture these rules rather than assume No Match means stop.

entries.title: Ask the right questions: the BA as translator
entries.text: Ask the right questions: the BA as translator Foundations A payments BA works with many stakeholders at once, from compliance and business teams to developers and vendors, across several projects and dependent systems. The work starts by asking whether each stakeholder understands the payment concepts, the sequence of payments, the business and its rules, and the payment journey, and whether the BA understands the system, the processing and where they fit in the flow. When a stakeholder does not know an answer, the BA helps them understand the question and reach it, because that translation is what makes the requirements workable, and asking the right questions is the core of stakeholder management, not a soft skill on the side. When a stakeholder does not know an answer, the BA helps them understand the question and reach it, because that translation is what makes the requirements workable, and asking the right questions is the core of stakeholder management, not a soft skill on the

entries.title: Account aggregator: your money stays with your bank
entries.text: Account aggregator: your money stays with your bank Foundations An account aggregator is not a bank and does not hold your money; it connects you to the financial institutions that do, giving you one dashboard across banks, mutual funds, insurers and NBFCs. Its three roles are pulling the data together, managing the customer consent before any access, and sharing the information with other financial institutions only with that consent. Apps like Paytm, PhonePe and Google Pay work the same way: they fetch and move money through your banks without holding it themselves. The single most important role of the aggregator is consent management, because it never holds the funds it connects you to. The single most important role of the aggregator is consent management, because it never holds the funds it connects you to.

entries.title: Three accounts, one place: what Open Banking allows
entries.text: Three accounts, one place: what Open Banking allows Foundations Open Banking uses APIs and the Account Information Service to let one app show accounts held at several banks, so a customer can see three accounts in one place without switching apps. An account aggregator combines those accounts into a single dashboard, and the aggregated data can also support payments and loan eligibility decisions. The test is whether the app reaches the banking information through open APIs; if it locks the data in instead, that is monetisation of a latch-on mechanism, not Open Banking. A customer should not need a new bank account merely to view other accounts. A customer should not need a new bank account merely to view other accounts.

entries.title: Open Banking is accounts; Open Finance is the whole life
entries.text: Open Banking is accounts; Open Finance is the whole life Foundations Open Banking lets one app show a customer bank accounts, track expenses, pay bills or apply for a loan, but it covers only bank accounts. Open Finance goes further, letting insurers, mutual fund companies and banks share information about investments, insurance, pensions and mortgages through APIs, always with the customer consent. Fintech apps like Paytm and PhonePe are not banks; they connect to banks to share account information, and Open Finance extends that same consented sharing beyond banking. The difference is scope: Open Banking is banking data, Open Finance is the customer whole financial life. The difference is scope: Open Banking is banking data, Open Finance is the customer whole financial life.

entries.title: BA duties across the delivery lifecycle
entries.text: BA duties across the delivery lifecycle Foundations The analyst owns the thread from discovery to live running: discovery establishes the business problem and the real users, analysis and design convert that understanding into testable requirements, and build and test keep the increment honest against what was agreed. After release the work is not over: the analyst validates the outcome in production and reports what remains open. A lifecycle without that closing loop leaves value unproven. A lifecycle without that closing loop leaves value unproven.

entries.title: The analyst inside an Agile Scrum sprint
entries.text: The analyst inside an Agile Scrum sprint Foundations In Scrum the analyst works the sprint, not around it: refinement turns vague stories into clear acceptance criteria, planning grounds scope and priority in what the team can actually deliver, and delivery is a running conversation as detail emerges. Review and acceptance close the loop by testing the built increment against the criteria agreed. An analyst who only appears at review is too late to shape anything. An analyst who only appears at review is too late to shape anything.

entries.title: Functional and non-functional requirements
entries.text: Functional and non-functional requirements Foundations Functional requirements state what the system must do, such as validating a payment or posting a ledger entry, while non-functional requirements state how well it must do it: performance, security, availability, usability and supportability. Both belong in the specification as explicit, testable statements, because a payment that is correct yet too slow or unavailable still fails the customer. Function without fitness for use is not a working payment. Function without fitness for use is not a working payment.

entries.title: User story or use case: choosing the form
entries.text: User story or use case: choosing the form Foundations A user story is outcome led: it states what a user wants to achieve and why, which makes it the right tool for prioritisation and conversation. A use case is interaction led: it pins down steps, actors and outcomes for one interaction, including decisions and exception paths. Choose by the need in front of you, not by team habit. The wrong form hides the detail that matters. The wrong form hides the detail that matters.

entries.title: BRD, FRD and use case: picking the artefact
entries.text: BRD, FRD and use case: picking the artefact Foundations The business requirements document states what the business needs and why, the functional requirements document states in detail what the system must do, and a use case describes one specific interaction between actors and the system. Selection turns on audience, complexity, traceability and delivery context, so each reader gets the detail they need and nothing they do not. The right artefact is the one its reader can act on. The right artefact is the one its reader can act on.

entries.title: Post-deployment reporting that stakeholders use
entries.text: Post-deployment reporting that stakeholders use Foundations After release, stakeholders need one factual, regular report covering adoption, incidents, defects, service levels, benefits realised and open risks. Adoption shows whether the change is used, incidents and defects show what is still broken, service levels show whether it performs, and benefits and open risks show whether the intended outcome is on track. A report built this way lets stakeholders decide what needs attention next. Reporting that hides the open items is worse than no report at all. Reporting that hides the open items is worse than no report at all.

entries.title: Presenting change in business value terms
entries.text: Presenting change in business value terms Foundations Stakeholders decide on outcomes, not on technical detail, so present the change in their terms: the outcome it delivers, the customer impact, the revenue or cost effect, the compliance position, the timing and the decisions needed. Keep the language plain and tie every point to something the stakeholder is accountable for. A case argued on value gets decided; a case argued on features gets deferred. A case argued on value gets decided; a case argued on features gets deferred.

entries.title: Incident status support teams can repeat
entries.text: Incident status support teams can repeat Foundations During an incident, support needs a status it can repeat to customers without guessing: the symptom in plain language, the users affected, a workaround if one exists, the owner, the severity and the time of the next update. Update at the promised time even if nothing has changed, because silence makes customers assume the worst. Reliable updates are part of the fix, not an extra. Reliable updates are part of the fix, not an extra.

entries.title: Written records and sign-offs that protect delivery
entries.text: Written records and sign-offs that protect delivery Foundations Written communication is the record that protects a delivery: meeting notes name the action, the owner and the due date, decisions are recorded with the assumptions behind them, and approval is obtained explicitly rather than inferred from silence. A sign-off only works if it states exactly what was approved and by whom, leaving no room for a later dispute about scope. If it is not written down, it was not agreed. If it is not written down, it was not agreed.

entries.title: Payment gateway versus payment processor
entries.text: Payment gateway versus payment processor Foundations The gateway orchestrates the payment: it connects the merchant to the payment methods, routes the instruction and returns the outcome. The processor performs the transaction processing: it moves the instruction through authorisation, clearing and settlement with the scheme and the banks. Some providers do both, so check which role a provider actually performs before assuming what it is responsible for. Confusing the two roles means blaming the wrong party when a payment fails. Confusing the two roles means blaming the wrong party when a payment fails.

entries.title: Seven causes behind payment failures
entries.text: Seven causes behind payment failures Foundations Payment failures classify into a small set of causes: issuer declines, validation failures, limit failures, timeout failures, connectivity failures, risk failures and downstream processing failures. An issuer decline refuses authorisation, a validation failure means the instruction is incomplete or wrong, a limit failure means an amount or frequency limit is exceeded, a timeout means no response arrived in time, a connectivity failure means a link dropped, a risk failure means a fraud or sanctions screen blocked the payment, and a downstream failure happens after acceptance. Classifying correctly decides who must act and what the customer should be told. Classifying correctly decides who must act and what the customer should be told.

entries.title: Turning prior experience into BA value
entries.text: Turning prior experience into BA value Foundations Moving into business analysis from another domain works when transferable skills are mapped to the work an analyst actually does: experience in operations, support or product maps to domain knowledge, elicitation, documentation, delivery support and outcome measurement. State the mapping explicitly, with concrete examples of work done, rather than listing a previous job title and hoping the reader makes the connection. A mapped skill is a hiring argument; an unmapped job title is just a label. A mapped skill is a hiring argument; an unmapped job title is just a label.

entries.title: Pick a BA domain before learning tools
entries.text: Pick a BA domain before learning tools Foundations Before learning tools, choose the domain to work in, weighing transferable experience, demand for the domain, genuine interest and a realistic entry path. An analyst is hired for domain understanding first and tool skill second, so a focused domain choice makes learning faster and a profile credible to a recruiter in that domain. Tools are easy to learn; credibility in a domain is what gets the interview. Tools are easy to learn; credibility in a domain is what gets the interview.

entries.title: Making a profile visible to recruiter search
entries.text: Making a profile visible to recruiter search Foundations Recruiters search by keywords that match the role they are filling, so align profile keywords with the target role, the domain, the skills and the verifiable experience, and a search for that role will surface the profile. Claim only what can be evidenced, because a keyword that cannot be backed up damages credibility in the first conversation. Visibility gets the call; evidence wins it. Visibility gets the call; evidence wins it.

entries.title: Answering honestly when you do not know
entries.text: Answering honestly when you do not know Foundations In an interview, not knowing an answer is acceptable if it is handled honestly: state the assumptions being made, explain the reasoning that follows from them, and identify what would need to be validated before committing to an answer. Never bluff. Interviewers test judgement and honesty as much as knowledge, and a confident guess that turns out wrong is worse than a clear statement of what is known and what is not. Interviewers test judgement and honesty as much as knowledge, and a confident guess that turns out wrong is worse than a clear statement of what is known and what is not.

entries.title: Working through an unfamiliar scenario
entries.text: Working through an unfamiliar scenario Foundations Face an unfamiliar scenario in a fixed order: clarify the assumptions, break the flow into its stages, identify the risks at each stage, and state what evidence would be obtained before deciding. This structure shows clear thinking even when the domain is new, and it prevents the answer from becoming a guess. Method is what carries you when knowledge runs out. Method is what carries you when knowledge runs out.

entries.title: Serial versus cover: two ways funds move
entries.text: Serial versus cover: two ways funds move Foundations The serial method moves funds and payment information together down one chain, each bank passing the same instruction onward to the next. The cover method splits them: the instruction travels in an MT103 while the funds settle separately through an MT202 COV, so each leg is settled on its own. The method chosen governs tracking, charging and returns, so it must be identified before any of those are handled. The method chosen governs tracking, charging and returns, so it must be identified before any of those are handled.

entries.title: MT202 COV is not a plain MT202
entries.text: MT202 COV is not a plain MT202 Foundations An MT202 COV exists to settle a specific MT103: it moves the funds for that customer payment and carries the reference that binds the two messages together. A plain MT202 is a bank's own transfer, moving proprietary funds between banks with no customer payment behind it. Both move money between banks, yet only the COV answers to a customer instruction, and that distinction is what trips people up. Both move money between banks, yet only the COV answers to a customer instruction, and that distinction is what trips people up.

entries.title: Why banks split information from funds
entries.text: Why banks split information from funds Foundations The cover method separates the payment instruction from the funds so the MT103 can reach the beneficiary bank fast while settlement works through correspondent accounts at its own pace. Keeping customer details out of the funds leg also protects privacy and keeps the correspondent chain clean. The price is reconciliation: the two legs must match on amount and reference, and any mismatch becomes an exception. The price is reconciliation: the two legs must match on amount and reference, and any mismatch becomes an exception.

entries.title: MT103 pays customers, MT202 moves bank funds
entries.text: MT103 pays customers, MT202 moves bank funds Foundations An MT103 is a customer payment instruction: it orders the receiving bank to pay a named beneficiary a named amount. An MT202 is a bank-to-bank instruction that moves funds between banks with no customer beneficiary attached. Every customer payment starts with an MT103, and an MT202 appears only when a separate funds leg is required. Every customer payment starts with an MT103, and an MT202 appears only when a separate funds leg is required.

entries.title: Reading an MT103: fields 59 and 57
entries.text: Reading an MT103: fields 59 and 57 Foundations Field 59 names the beneficiary customer and the account to be credited, so it is the first field to check when a payment must reach the right person. Field 57 names the beneficiary bank by BIC, telling the chain which bank must receive the instruction. In a serial payment each bank reads both fields from the MT103 it receives and forwards the message to the next bank in the chain. In a serial payment each bank reads both fields from the MT103 it receives and forwards the message to the next bank in the chain.

entries.title: MT103 fields 50 and 72: who pays, what else
entries.text: MT103 fields 50 and 72: who pays, what else Foundations Field 50 identifies the ordering customer, the party who instructed the payment, and it is the first field screening and reconciliation check. Field 72 carries sender-to-receiver information, the extra instructions that fit no structured field. The two fields answer different questions: field 50 says who is paying, field 72 says what else the receiver needs to know. The two fields answer different questions: field 50 says who is paying, field 72 says what else the receiver needs to know.

entries.title: SDD Core versus SDD B2B: the refund divide
entries.text: SDD Core versus SDD B2B: the refund divide Foundations SDD Core covers collections from consumers and businesses, and it gives the debtor an eight-week refund right with no reason required. SDD B2B is restricted to business-to-business collections and grants no such refund right, which is why the debtor bank must verify the mandate before the first collection. The schemes differ on refunds and mandate checks, so using the wrong one is a real error, not a paperwork slip. The schemes differ on refunds and mandate checks, so using the wrong one is a real error, not a paperwork slip.

entries.title: A SEPA payment is defined by its scheme
entries.text: A SEPA payment is defined by its scheme Foundations A SEPA payment is defined by scheme rules on timing, reason codes and returns, not by the message format that happens to carry it. The format is only the envelope: the same payment can be initiated with an MT101 or an MT103 as well as with a pain.001. That is why an MT103 and a pacs.008 can carry one underlying SEPA payment, the pacs.008 being its ISO 20022 form. That is why an MT103 and a pacs.008 can carry one underlying SEPA payment, the pacs.008 being its ISO 20022 form.

entries.title: pacs.004 returns, camt.056 recalls
entries.text: pacs.004 returns, camt.056 recalls Foundations A pacs.004 returns a payment that has already settled, sending the funds back along the chain to the originator. A camt.056 requests a recall, asking the beneficiary bank to return a payment already credited. The two are often confused, yet they do opposite jobs: the pacs.004 moves the money back, while the camt.056 asks for the money back. The two are often confused, yet they do opposite jobs: the pacs.004 moves the money back, while the camt.056 asks for the money back.

entries.title: Catching a duplicate pacs.008
entries.text: Catching a duplicate pacs.008 Foundations Every payment inside a pacs.008 file carries its own unique identification, and that identifier is the control that catches a file containing the same transaction twice before it is processed. The check matters because a bulk file such as a pain.001 can carry one instruction more than once, and paying it twice is a real loss. Duplicate detection is therefore a pre-processing discipline, not a post-payment investigation. Duplicate detection is therefore a pre-processing discipline, not a post-payment investigation.

entries.title: MT to MX: the same legs, new names
entries.text: MT to MX: the same legs, new names Foundations A pacs.008 is the ISO 20022 customer credit transfer, the equivalent of an MT103, and a pacs.009 is the financial institution credit transfer, the equivalent of an MT202. A pacs.004 is the payment return, used when a pacs.008 cannot be applied and the funds must go back. The two families describe the same payments, so a team moving from MT to MX only has to learn the new names for the same legs. The two families describe the same payments, so a team moving from MT to MX only has to learn the new names for the same legs.

entries.title: Corporates instruct with MT101, banks pay
entries.text: Corporates instruct with MT101, banks pay Foundations A corporation connected to SWIFT instructs its bank with an MT101, and it is the bank that sends the MT103, or the MT103 plus an MT202 COV, into the interbank chain. Even a corporate with its own BIC and a direct relationship with a clearer does not send an MT103 itself. The rule is simple: corporates instruct, banks pay. The rule is simple: corporates instruct, banks pay.

entries.title: Nostro and vostro: one account, two names
entries.text: Nostro and vostro: one account, two names Foundations When a bank holds an account with another bank in a foreign currency, it calls that account a nostro account, meaning our account with you. The bank that holds the account calls the very same account a vostro account, meaning your account with us. There is only one account, and the two words simply say which side of it each bank is standing on. There is only one account, and the two words simply say which side of it each bank is standing on.

entries.title: Block 2: input or output depends on your side
entries.text: Block 2: input or output depends on your side Foundations Block 2 of a SWIFT message, the application header, says whether the message is entering or leaving the SWIFT network. The same payment looks different from the two sides: from the sending bank it is an input message, and from the receiving bank it is an output message. An operator reading a stored message must therefore know which bank's copy it is looking at before deciding what block 2 means. An operator reading a stored message must therefore know which bank's copy it is looking at before deciding what block 2 means.

entries.title: One MT103, one beneficiary
entries.text: One MT103, one beneficiary Foundations An MT103 carries a single beneficiary in field 59, so one message pays one beneficiary at one bank. A payment that must reach a seller and a manufacturer at different banks needs two separate MT103 messages, one for each beneficiary. Trying to name two beneficiaries in a single MT103 is not possible, because the message has nowhere to put the second one. Trying to name two beneficiaries in a single MT103 is not possible, because the message has nowhere to put the second one.

entries.title: Field 32A: value date, currency, settlement amount
entries.text: Field 32A: value date, currency, settlement amount Foundations Field 32A carries three things: the value date in year-month-day order, the currency, and the interbank settlement amount. The value date is the date the funds are to be available to the receiver, not the date the message was sent. The currency in field 32A is the currency the receiver's bank actually receives, which is why it can differ from the currency the ordering customer instructed in field 33B. The currency in field 32A is the currency the receiver's bank actually receives, which is why it can differ from the currency the ordering customer instructed in field 33B.

entries.title: The restricted SWIFT character set
entries.text: The restricted SWIFT character set Foundations SWIFT MT messages use a restricted character set, and characters outside it cannot be used in a message at all. That is why country-specific characters, such as Japanese or Thai script, cannot appear in an MT101 or an MT103, even when the underlying instruction is domestic. Names and addresses must be written with the characters the SWIFT set allows, or the message will not be accepted. Names and addresses must be written with the characters the SWIFT set allows, or the message will not be accepted.

entries.title: MT101: one message for three kinds of transfer
entries.text: MT101: one message for three kinds of transfer Foundations An MT101 can move funds between an ordering customer's own accounts, in favour of a third party domestically, and in favour of a third party internationally. All three uses are valid, because the message is a general request for transfer, not a payment for one kind of beneficiary. The same message therefore serves a corporate moving money between its own accounts and a corporate paying a supplier abroad. The same message therefore serves a corporate moving money between its own accounts and a corporate paying a supplier abroad.

entries.title: SCT: a pacs.002 rejection stops at the CSM
entries.text: SCT: a pacs.002 rejection stops at the CSM Foundations In a SEPA credit transfer, the pacs.008 passes through the clearing and settlement mechanism on its way to the beneficiary bank, and the mechanism validates it against its own rules. A failure at that stage comes back as a pacs.002, so the payment never reaches the beneficiary bank and that bank stays unaware of it.
